content.title: Sporting CP-Bodø/Glimt - UEFA Champions League - 2026
content.text: Watch: Lamine Yamal, Mohamed Salah, Raphinha and Mathys Tel feature in our compilation of the best assists from the UEFA Champions League round of 16 second legs.4Watch: Thibaut Courtois and Gianluigi Donnarumma feature in our compilation of tonight's best UEFA Champions League saves.4Watch: Francisco Trincão spoke to UEFA following Sporting CP's comeback win against Bodø/Glimt to reach the Champions League quarter-finals.7Sporting CP's quarter-final opponents have been confirmed as Arsenal after the Gunners beat Leverkusen 3-1 on aggregate. 8Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeFinally from Rui Borges: "True champions rise to the occasion. This team's resilience is unshakeable and boundless. Their resilience and ambition know no bounds, and they proved it today. The team knew exactly what they had to do; the energy was there, and every single player played a vital role. They were completely in sync."26More from Rui Borges: "With the fans’ support, I also felt it was going to be a different night. Even if we'd only won 2-0, I'd be standing here feeling incredibly proud of everything. More than any strategy, it has a lot to do with belief, with the determination and intensity we put into the game."19Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeRui Borges, Sporting coach, to SportTV: "We knew the best Bodø/Glimt, but we were the best Sporting. I felt we were connected from the very first moment we returned to training. The energy was different; the desire to do something different was boundless."16Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeMore from Kjetil Knutsen: "I can't really put my finger on why we ended up like that, but there were only brief spells where we managed to put anything together. We were a long way off our identity and what we're supposed to be."8Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeKjetil Knutsen, Bodø/Glimt coach, speaking to TV 2: "We did not play the game, we played the occasion, and it became far too big for us. Sporting CP went out there and didn't care about anything, while we were thinking about the consequences from the very first touch. That made us passive."12Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeMore from Patrick Berg: "We had a game plan, but we did not really manage to stick to it, and it all became a bit in-between. Unfortunately, then we ended up being a worse version of ourselves."8Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladePatrick Berg, Bodø/Glimt midfielder, speaking to TV 2: "It feels really tough right now. Sporting were sharp when they managed to get into the second spaces and play the ball in behind our defence. Of course, they played a very good match. But first and foremost, we have to focus on ourselves and evaluate what we could have done better, because there's no doubt that our performance was far below the level we expect". 7Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeMore from Francisco Trincão: "We believed in it [the comeback] from the very first minute; the manager made us believe in it too. Everyone believed, and the fans also gave us that energy throughout the match. As time went on, we realised we were capable of it and saw it through to the end. We’ve achieved something historic."14Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeFrancisco Trincão, Sporting forward and Player of the Match, to SportTV: "What matters is the team's victory; we had the intensity, the momentum and the energy that we lacked in the first match. We always believed – the manager, us and the fans. We got the pressure right; we pressed harder and better, we had a different energy, a different intensity – we’d been warned about Bodø's style of play."17Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeMore from Maxi Araújo on his goal: "It was undoubtedly the most important goal of my career – a Champions League goal, here at home. I'd like to thank my family, and my wife, who's up there in the stands and has always given me so much support, no matter what."17Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeMaxi Araújo, Sporting defender: "There was a lot of scepticism as people thought it was almost impossible, but we showed that we believed in ourselves and turned it around. We played a perfect game; we had to give it our all. Everyone was focused on winning and turning it around – we're Sporting, we had to do it, and we did!"14Credit to Bodø, who have enjoyed an unforgettable debut Champions League campaign, surprising many along the way to get this far. Tonight, however, was not their night. 39Carlos MachadoReporting from Estádio José AlvaladeSporting have won all five of their home matches at Estádio José Alvalade in this season’s Champions League: 4–1 vs Kairat, 2–1 vs Marseille, 3–0 vs Club Brugge, 2–1 vs Paris and now 5–0 vs Bodø/Glimt. It's become quite a fortress for the Lisbon side.22Sporting CP will now face the winners of Arsenal vs Leverkusen in the quarter-finals, with the first leg taking place on 7/8 April and the return on 14/15 April. 34
